passages.quote:
Transparency in supply chains: a practical guide

Section 54 of the Modern Slavery Act 2015 requires certain organisations to develop a modern slavery statement each year.

The modern slavery statement should set out what steps organisations have taken to ensure modern slavery is not taking place in their business or supply chains.

This document provides guidance on:

who is required to publish a modern slavery statement

how to write a modern slavery statement

how to approve and publish the statement

actions businesses should consider to tackle modern slavery

International reporting template on modern slavery, forced labour and child labour

The UK, Australian and Canadian governments recognise that many organisations operating internationally are subject to modern slavery reporting requirements in all 3 countries.

This optional template is designed to reduce the administrative burden for organisations subject to supply chain reporting requirements in the UK, Australia and Canada. It supports the development of 1 report for all 3 countries.

This template aligns with the transparency in supply chains guidance above but has different reporting categories to accommodate for Australian and Canadian legislation.

This document is the product of collaboration with the Australian and Canadian governments through the ‘Principles to Guide Governmental Action to Combat Human Trafficking in Global Supply Chains’ group.

We are aware this publication may have accessibility issues, for example if you use assistive technology.

Contact us if you need this document in a different format.
